newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina plans to sign Cambodian oil agreement.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina plans to sign Cambodian oil agreement.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said on Tuesday it planned to sign a memorandum of understanding with the Cambodian government later this month to cooperate in developing its oil sector.
"We expect to sign the MOU with Cambodia this month to cooperate in the upstream and downstream oil sector there," Pertamina president director Faisal Abda'oe told reporters.
It is expected to coincide with a planned visit by Indonesian President Suharto to Burma, Cambodia and Laos. The dates of the visit have not yet been finalised.
Abda'oe said the Cambodian government has long sought Pertamina's help to develop its oil and gas sector, including training for Cambodian workers in this industry.
Another Pertamina official, who asked not to be named, said prospects were good for oil and gas in Cambodia.

"Pertamina hopes it can participate in one of the areas in Cambodia which is a good prospect. This is part of Pertamina's strategy to participate in the search for oil reserves abroad," the official said. He gave no other details.
Last November, Pertamina signed an agreement to cooperate in the oil sector with the Burmese government.
